findings.title: Light-theme value silently changed from 30% to 70% for topic-meta-data h5 a
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`. The light-theme arm now uses 70% instead of the original 30%, so embedded-post author links become much lighter on light themes. This is a regression in the very theme the PR is not meant to affect. The light arm should stay at 30%, and the dark arm should then be 70% to match the pattern.

findings.title: Light-theme lightness for .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule uses `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 50%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 50%))`. This changes the light-theme appearance by making the name lighter and giving it the same color as `.title`, which removes the visual distinction between name and title. The light arm should be 30% and the dark arm `$secondary` 70%, consistent with `.user-small .name` elsewhere in this PR.

findings.title: Light-theme lightness for mobile .group-member-info .name changed from 30% to 50%
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%)`. The new rule uses 50%/50%, which alters the light-theme look and makes `.name` identical to `.title`. This is a copy/paste error. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`.

findings.title: Light-theme value for .custom-message-length changed from 70% to 30%
findings.body: The original rule was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%)`. The new rule is `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 30%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 70%))`. The light arm was swapped from 70% to 30% and the dark arm uses 70%, so the pair is inverted. On light themes the text is much darker than before, and on dark themes it is brighter than the desktop equivalent. The desktop version of the same rule correctly uses 70% / 30%. This should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 70%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 30%))`.

findings.title: Light-theme value for .topic-map h3 changed from 20% to 50%
findings.body: The original color was `scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%)`. The new rule uses 50%/50%, which makes the topic-map heading as faint as the h4 below it on light themes. This is a regression in the light theme and loses the heading/subheading hierarchy. It should be `dark-light-choose(scale-color($primary, $lightness: 20%), scale-color($secondary, $lightness: 80%))`, matching the `.number, i` rule in the same file.
